unitsPage.title: Exam Units — Capable & Proficient
unitsPage.intro: The four units examined for Capable and Proficient phases. Each unit has its own vocabulary themes. Master vocab for the unit you're tested on and your speaking topic.
unitsPage.notice: These are the actual units from your G9 French revision list.

unite1.title: Unité 1 — Quels sont les facteurs de la bonne santé ?
vocab: Une alimentation saine — healthy eating
La malbouffe — junk food
L'obésité et la sous-alimentation — obesity and undernutrition
Avoir un style de vie sain — to have a healthy lifestyle
Chez le médecin — at the doctor's (Proficient)
La santé et mon environnement — health and my environment (Proficient)

unite2.title: Unité 2 — Qu'est-ce que la solidarité humaine et le service à la communauté ?
vocab: La solidarité — solidarity. Comment être solidaire — how to show solidarity
Les types de solidarité — forms of mutual support; use the categories defined in your course.
Les dix qualités du profil de l’apprenant de l’IB — the ten IB learner profile attributes.
Les types de communauté — types of community
Mon projet de service à la communauté — my community service project
Les associations solidaires mondiales — global solidarity associations

unite3.title: Unité 3 — Es-tu curieux ? (vacances & tourisme)
vocab: Les vacances — holidays
Les moyens de transport — means of transport
Le tourisme de masse — mass tourism
Le tourisme durable — sustainable tourism (Proficient)
Les activités de vacances — holiday activities
Les différents types de vacances — different types of holiday
La francophonie — the Francophone world (Proficient)
La migration — migration (Proficient)

unite4.title: Unité 4 — L'éducation pour tous, l'éducation pour la paix
vocab: Une journée typique à l’école — a typical school day.
L'école du futur — the school of the future
Le système éducatif français — the French education system
Le droit à l'éducation — the right to education
Les élèves dans le monde francophone — students in the Francophone world
'Sur le chemin de l'école' (film) — On the Way to School (documentary)
Malala — referenced education-rights activist
Ça sert à quoi l'école? Projets d'avenir — what is school for? Future plans

grammar.title: Grammar checklist (both phases)
items: Les connecteurs logiques — donc, parce que, cependant, en effet, ainsi
Le comparatif et le superlatif — plus…que / moins…que / le plus / le moins
Verbes (régulier et irrégulier) au présent
Opinions et justifications — je pense que, à mon avis, selon moi
Le passé composé + L'imparfait
Le conditionnel + Les hypothèses (si + imparfait, conditionnel)
Le futur proche / le futur simple
Proficient extras: le gérondif (en + -ant); avant de + infinitif; après avoir / être + participe passé; les verbes impersonnels (il faut que, il est nécessaire que); le subjonctif

emergent.title: Emergent phase — your 4 units
items: Unité 1 — Mon identité, mes préférences, ma culture (famille, loisirs, alimentation, célébrations)
Unité 2 — Suis-je responsable de mon environnement ? (types de pollution, causes, conséquences, actions)
Unité 3 — Es-tu curieux ? (pays, villes, transport, vacances, saisons)
Unité 4 — À quoi sert l'école ? (matières, routine, professions, uniforme, plans d'études)

textTypesPage.title: Text Types for Written Production
textTypesPage.intro: Common written forms and useful conventions. Adapt them to the audience, purpose and task; the channel (print, website or email) does not determine the register.

discours.title: Le discours (Speech)
discours.body: A speech (discours) is written to be delivered to listeners. It may inform, explain or persuade; its vocabulary and form of address should suit the audience.
conventions: Greet the audience and establish your topic and purpose.
Use je, nous or direct address when appropriate; a speech need not be entirely in first person.
Use vous for an audience of several people or a formal occasion; tu suits one familiar listener.
Develop a few connected points, each with a reason and a concrete example or checked evidence.
Rhetorical questions, repetition and imperatives are persuasive devices; use them deliberately, not in every sentence.
End by summing up the main points, returning to your purpose, then thanking the audience or offering a relevant next step.
Open with an attention device: a question, a striking statistic, a surprising fact or a short anecdote; humour works only if it does not distract from your purpose.
phrases: Mesdames et messieurs, chers professeurs, chers camarades… (ladies and gentlemen, dear teachers, dear classmates)
Merci d'être venus ce soir assister à… (thank you for coming this evening to attend…)
C'est un honneur pour moi d'être ici aujourd'hui. (it is an honour for me to be here today)
Nous sommes rassemblés / réunis ici aujourd'hui pour… (we have gathered here today to…)
Avant de commencer, je vous prie d'éteindre vos portables. (before we start, please switch off your mobile phones)
M'entendez-vous tous bien au fond de la salle ? (can everyone hear me clearly at the back of the room?)
J'aimerais vous parler aujourd'hui d'un sujet qui nous concerne tous. (today I would like to talk to you about a subject that concerns us all)
Je peux maintenant répondre à vos questions. (I can now answer your questions)
Merci de votre attention / Je vous remercie. (thank you for your attention)

article.title: L'article (Article)
article.body: An article is a text for a print or online publication about an event, facts or a point of view. A report, feature and opinion column have different purposes; identify the type the task requests before choosing structure and register.
conventions: A clear title; a byline and date when the task calls for them.
A chapeau is a short introductory summary beneath the title; it differs from an image caption (légende).
Paragraphs and optional subheadings organise the material.
Attribute quotations, statistics and claims to real sources; do not invent evidence.
The conditional can report an unconfirmed claim, as in il aurait quitté la ville; make clear that the claim is not yet confirmed.
Images and captions are optional features of the publication, not required in every article.

Open with a hook or a short quotation. Use témoignages (first-hand accounts), direct questions and exclamations only where they suit the tone. Report what people said with verbs such as a déclaré que or a dénoncé, and use guillemets (« ») for quotations.
phrases: D’après [titre et date de l’étude], … (according to [title and date of the study], …)
La personne interrogée explique que… (the person interviewed explains that…)
Ces résultats suggèrent que… (these results suggest that…)
Ces informations restent à confirmer. (this information still needs to be confirmed)

lettre.title: La lettre officielle (Formal letter)
lettre.body: A formal letter addresses an institution or person in a professional or official relationship. State the purpose clearly and use a suitable greeting, organised paragraphs and courteous closing.
conventions: Identify sender and recipient and include the date when required. Layout varies by convention or template.
Objet : a concise statement of the subject.
Greeting: Madame, Monsieur, or a suitable form with the recipient's name or title.
Body: purpose, relevant details and the requested response.
Closing: for example, Je vous prie d’agréer, Madame, Monsieur, l’expression de mes salutations distinguées (roughly: yours faithfully).
Signature.

blog.title: Le blog (Blog post)
blog.body: A blog post is an entry in an online publication. It can be personal or professional. First person and a conversational style are possible choices, not requirements.

courriel.title: Le courriel / l'email
courriel.body: Courriel (email) is an electronic message. Use a clear subject, greeting, concise paragraphs and sign-off. It may be formal or informal depending on purpose and relationship, just like a letter.

extras.title: French — Extras
extras.intro: Topics beyond the G9 syllabus — subjunctive, idioms, francophone culture.

subjunctive.title: Subjunctive mood — quick intro
subjunctive.body: The subjunctive is a mood, not a time reference. It often appears after expressions of wish, doubt or necessity and conjunctions such as bien que: il faut que tu finisses. Affirmative je pense que normally takes the indicative: je pense qu’il vient. For many verbs use the ils present stem for je/tu/il/ils and the nous present stem for nous/vous, with -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent. Être, avoir and other common verbs have irregular forms.

idioms.title: Idioms & expressions
items: Avoir le cafard — to feel blue (lit. 'to have the cockroach')
Coûter les yeux de la tête — to cost an arm and a leg (lit. 'cost the eyes of the head')
Tomber dans les pommes — to faint (lit. 'fall into the apples')
Poser un lapin — to stand someone up (lit. 'place a rabbit')
Avoir un chat dans la gorge — to have a frog in your throat (lit. 'have a cat in your throat')
Ce n'est pas la mer à boire — it's not that hard (lit. 'it's not the sea to drink')
Mettre son grain de sel — to add one's two cents (lit. 'add one's grain of salt')

culture.title: Francophone culture
culture.body: Francophone means French-speaking. Lower-case francophonie can refer to French speakers and their cultural or linguistic communities; the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) is a particular international organisation. French is used in many countries and regions, with varied accents, vocabulary and multilingual settings; these uses cannot be reduced to France alone.

literature.title: Classic French literature
items: Le Petit Prince (Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, 1943) — a tale exploring friendship, responsibility and adult values.
Les Misérables (Victor Hugo, 1862) — epic novel of redemption and rebellion
Madame Bovary (Gustave Flaubert, 1856) — pioneering realist novel
L’Étranger (Albert Camus, 1942) — a novel exploring human life and the absurd.
Le Rouge et le Noir (Stendhal, 1830) — ambition and society

filmMusic.title: Modern film & music
filmMusic.body: Films to explore: Amélie (2001), The Intouchables (2011), La Haine (1995). Singers: Stromae (Belgian), Aya Nakamura, Indila, Christine and the Queens. Watching/listening with French subtitles is a great way to train your ear.
